title: rhun extension manifest (extension.ini), protocol version 1.1
description: The manifest is an INI file (UTF-8, key = value, # comments, unknown keys ignored). This schema describes it as the object it maps to: top-level keys are properties of the root; dotted keys such as run.linux-x86_64 become the 'run' object with the part after the dot as the key; each [section] is an object of the same name ([settings] keeps its dotted KEY.FIELD keys as property names). Two rules the schema cannot state: 'name' must equal the folder's name and 'owner' the parent folder's name, and a target needs either a 'run' entry for it or 'runtime' with 'run'. Section 2 of v1.md says what each key means.

name.description: the extension's name, equal to its folder; commands are NAME.command

owner.description: the GitHub owner, equal to the parent folder

title.description: shown in Settings and after command titles

protocol.description: the protocol version this extension speaks

run.description: the program per target, relative to the extension folder (from the dotted keys run.TARGET; wasm32-wasip1 is a WebAssembly module rhun runs itself where no other target applies); or, with 'runtime', the single key 'run' at the top level is the script

runtime.description: a program found on PATH that runs the script named by 'run' (python3, node, …)

requires.description: shown when the runtime is missing or too old; not checked by rhun 0.18.0

args.description: extra arguments for the program, space separated

on.description: when the extension starts: startup (the default: an installed extension runs), command, project, lang:LANG, open:PATTERN; several, space separated; a manifest command always starts it

commands.description: [commands]: key = Title | default keys (space separated, each with a modifier; '|' and keys optional)

subscribe.description: [subscribe]: which events to send, with name patterns ('*' all, '*.go' a suffix, 'Makefile' an exact name, 'no' none); a document is reported only when 'opened' names it

needs.description: [needs]: the capabilities (section 5); a request without its capability is refused with 'needs'

run.description: programs the extension may start, by name, space separated

git.description: read the project's Git data through rhun (feature git-data); shown as 'read the project's Git history'

secrets.description: store passwords and tokens in the system keychain (feature secrets)

kernels.description: notebooks: programs rhun may start as the user for this extension's notebooks (nb-exec), names space separated

tests.description: Protocol 1.1: programs rhun may start for this extension as the user during a test run (test-exec): bare names, space separated, at most 16 of 64 bytes

debug.description: start the extension's debug adapters as the user, outside any sandbox, after one approval per project ([debugger.TYPE] sections)

description.description: one line shown on the Extensions page

icon.description: a PNG in the extension's folder (at most 64 KB and 256 pixels a side, square, 128 recommended): the badge in the title bar, its dropdown and the Extensions page, drawn on color

pack.description: a pack: other extensions installed with this one (at most 16, OWNER/NAME, space separated, not the pack itself). A pack needs no program: without run entries it never starts, and its themes and grammars load

views.description: [views] (protocol 1.1, feature view-tree): retained views as KEY.FIELD = VALUE, at most 16; place sidebar, panel or side; kind tree, or log with view-log; open yes expands it (sidebar) or chooses its tab the first time

settings.description: [settings]: the extension's own settings as KEY.FIELD = VALUE; shown on its page, sent as setting events (section 6d)

provides.description: [provides] (sections 12b to 12h): the files the extension serves each language feature in, name patterns as in [subscribe]; the provider hears opened and edits for them and is started by the first that opens. It must also say the feature after hello 1. Protocol 1.1 adds save_actions patterns; linked patterns (feature linked-editing); and the language features' keys (v1.1.md, Manifest keys), each read only when the feature named in its description was agreed.

complete.triggers.description: characters that ask for a list at once, space separated: '. :'

signature.triggers.description: characters that ask for signature help: '( ,'

actions.description: Code actions; requires negotiated actions, or code-actions (protocol 1.1: code-actions and code-action-resolve in place of actions)

rename.description: Rename Symbol; requires negotiated rename. With prepare-rename also agreed (protocol 1.1), F2 asks prepare-rename first

save_actions.description: Source code actions before saving; requires negotiated save-actions and documents=write.

notebook.description: Notebooks this extension reads and writes (feature notebooks): a matching file opens in a notebook tab.

notebook.title.description: The notebook format's name, as the user sees it.

editor.description: Files this extension edits in its own view (feature custom-editors).

editor.title.description: The editor's name, as Reopen With shows it.

editor.model.description: text: rhun keeps the file as a document; owned: the extension keeps it and saves it in parts.

editor.priority.description: default: matching files open in it; option: only through Reopen With.

notebook.kernel.description: yes: it runs cells (the default); no: a viewer or converter only.

commit_message.description: a commit-message provider (feature commit-message), listed in Settings > Git > Commit message AI

quickdiff.description: quick-diff bases (feature quickdiff) for files under roots the extension registers (scm-register), or outside any git repository

scm.description: a version control provider (feature scm): it registers Source Control tabs at run time

schemes.description: URI schemes whose documents it provides (feature uris), space separated: the extension name or NAME-x

agents.description: yes: the extension lists agent sessions in the agents panel (feature agents).

agents.title.description: the source's name on its rows and in Settings > Agents; the default is the extension's title

linked.description: protocol 1.1, feature linked-editing: the files the linked request is asked for

hover.description: the hover card; requires negotiated hover-query (rhun then asks hover-query in place of sending the v1 hover event)

declaration.description: Go to Declaration; requires negotiated navigation

type_definition.description: Go to Type Definition; requires negotiated navigation

implementation.description: Go to Implementation; requires negotiated navigation

selection_ranges.description: Expand and Shrink Selection; requires negotiated selection-ranges

call_hierarchy.description: the call hierarchy (call-hierarchy, then calls-in and calls-out about an item); requires negotiated hierarchy

type_hierarchy.description: the type hierarchy (type-hierarchy, then supertypes and subtypes about an item); requires negotiated hierarchy

workspace_symbols.description: Go to Symbol in Project, while a matching document is open; requires negotiated workspace-symbols

type_format.description: formatting as you type; requires negotiated partial-format

type_format.triggers.description: characters that ask for on-type formatting, space separated; the word newline stands for Enter: '; } newline'; requires negotiated partial-format

document_links.description: links under ctrl+hover; requires negotiated document-links

tests.description: Protocol 1.1: the files this test controller has tests in (feature tests).

tests.profiles.description: run kinds the controller offers besides run, space separated

tools.description: [tools] (feature tools): NAME = Title | description, with NAME.input (what the input holds) and NAME.readonly = yes (no confirmation before a call). NAME is 1 to 40 of [a-z0-9_]; at most 64 tools; texts are cut to 1000 bytes.

idle.description: stop: rhun stops the extension after idle.after seconds without work

idle.after.description: seconds without work before an idle = stop extension is stopped

runs.description: where it runs; both mean this computer in 0.18.0

command-options.description: [command-options] (protocol 1.1): per manifest command, NAME.icon (a built-in icon or ext:NAME from [icons]), NAME.when (enablement: a when clause), NAME.palette (no: not listed in the palette), NAME.callable (yes: other extensions may run-command it; needs command-args). A bad entry is dropped and listed on the extension's page.

keys.description: [keys] (protocol 1.1): KEYS = COMMAND [ARGS] [when CLAUSE]; KEYS one stroke or two separated by a space (ctrl+k ctrl+c), optionally prefixed linux:, mac: or windows:; COMMAND NAME (own), rhun.NAME or EXT.NAME / OWNER/EXT.NAME; ARGS (at most 4096 bytes) are the body of 0 run ... key LEN.

context.description: [context] (feature context-keys): defaults of the extension's keys for when clauses (OWNER/NAME.KEY), valid before the program starts and after it stops; at most 64 keys.

status.description: [status] (protocol 1.1): status bar items, ITEM.FIELD with FIELD text, tooltip, command (own command, run with FROM ref), args, align (left|right), priority (-1000..1000), color (fg muted accent error warning success), background (error|warning), when; at most 8 items with the runtime ones.

icons.description: [icons] (protocol 1.1): NAME = a PNG in the extension's folder (at most 65536 bytes, 256 pixels a side), used as ext:NAME in status items, menus and buttons; at most 32.

patterns.description: 'no', or space-separated name patterns: '*', '*.ext', an exact file name

^(menu\\.(editor|explorer|tab|terminal|e.description: [menu.LOCATION] and [submenu.NAME] (protocol 1.1): ITEM.command (a command as [keys] names it), ITEM.submenu (a [submenu.NAME]), ITEM.group, ITEM.order, ITEM.when, ITEM.args; [submenu.NAME] also has title. At most 16 items per extension per location.

^debugger\\.[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$.description: [debugger.TYPE]: a debug adapter rhun starts and speaks DAP to (feature debug); needs [needs] debug = yes

program.description: names tried in order on the login PATH and in paths, or a path inside the extension's folder
